newsitem.title: USA: Virco says ends talks with Mexico buyer.
newsitem.headline: Virco says ends talks with Mexico buyer.

text.p: Virco Corp Thursday said negotiations with the potential buyer of the Virco Mexican facility were terminated.

Virco said it decided to discontinue production at the facility effective August 30, 1997 and to sell the machinery, equipment and real estate. As a result of the shutdown the company expects to incur a pretax loss of approximately $3 million, which will be included in the second quarter financial results.
Virco reported first quarter net income of $499,000 vs. a $1,439,000 loss in the same period last year.

For the quarter, earnings per share improved by $.32 to $.08 per share versus a $.24 per share loss for the same period last year. Revenues for the quarter increased 11% to $40,958,000 compared to $36,745,000 a year ago.

"Raw material prices continue to be stable; plant efficiency, especially at our Torrance facility continues to improve; and the effect of increased prices in the company's markets along with better product mix also continue to increase our gross margin," said president Robert Virtue.
Gross margin level was 32.2% versus 25.5% in the first quarter of last year.

Virtue said that while he was disappointed with the loss from the Mexican plant disposition, he was extremely satisfied with the improvement in U.S. operations and believes that continuing progress will be made as a result of the consolidation of operations in the two U.S. facilities.
